Μύκονος.definition: Myconus, one of the Cyclades, Hdt.6.118, etc.; the people were said to be all bald, Lucil.1211, Str.10.5.9: whence the proverb 'it's all one, all alike', Plu.2.616b, Them.Or.21.250c, Zen.5.17 , prob. cj. in Luc.DMort.…

μυκτήρ.definition: from the use of the nose to express ridicule, sneerer, of Socrates, Timo25; in the abstract, sarcasm, raillery, Longin.34.2, cf. Plu.2.860e; Luc.Prom.Es1; AP9.188

μυλλός.definition: awry, crooked, Hsch. ; squint-eyed, Eust.906.54; cake in the shape of pudenda muliebria, Heraclid. Syrac. ap. Ath.14.647a

μύλος.definition: = mill, LXXEx.11.5, Plu.2.549d; millstone, PCair. Zen.355.84 , AP11.253 ; LXX2 Ki.11.21; Ev. Matt.18.6, Ev.Marc.9.42; Str.4.1.13: metaph., App.Prov.4.48: generally, stone, Hp.Steril.241

μυξάριον.definition: Dim. of I, M.Ant.4.48; Dim. of , Aët.5.118, Hsch. ; interpol. in D.S.1.34

μύουρος.definition: tapering (lit. mouse-; 'tapering' hexameters, in which the first syllable of one of the last two feet is short instead of long, Ath.14.632e, cf. Sch.Heph.p.290 C., Eust.900.7

μυρίαθλος.definition: poet. hero of myriad contests, Orac. ap.D.Chr.31.97

Μυρικαῖος.definition: epith. of Apollo in Lesbos, Sch.Nic.Th.613

μύρκος.definition: Syrac. word for dumb, Hsch.:—also Id

μυρμηδών.definition: ant's nest, Hsch.: Dor. for ant, Id., Gloss

μύρμηξ.definition: Dor. ant, Hes.Frr.14.5, 76.4, Theoc.9.31, 15.45, 17.107, etc.: metaph., Aeschrio2. 2. = II.2, Ar.Th.100. II. fabulous animal in India, Hdt.3.102; Str.2.1.9; Id.16.4.15, cf. Agatharch.69, Ael.NA3.4. III. hidden rock in…

Μυρρινοῦς.definition: name of a deme of Attica, Str.9.1.22: an inhabitant of it, IG12.335.42, Aeschin.1.98, etc.:— but another deme, IG2.872, 22.896.45, al

μυρσινοειδής.definition: myrtle-like, h.Merc.81, cf; Medic., shaped like a myrtle leaf, of an incision, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23.47, Aët.15.5. Adv. Heliod. ap. Orib.44.8.24, Gal.10.886, Hippiatr.16

μυρτίδανον.definition: a myrtle-like plant, Hp.Mul.1.34; warty excrescence on the stem of the myrtle, like the kermes berries on the holm-oak, Dsc.1.112, Plin.HN23.164

μύρτον.definition: myrtle-berry, Pherecr.148, Ar.Av.160, 1100; pudenda muliebria, Ar.Lys.1004, Ruf.Onom.111, Poll.2.174

μύσις.definition: Ion. closing, Aret.SD2.1, cf. Dsc.1.32 ; Gal.6.218, 7.249, 10.602

μύσος.definition: uncleanness, defilement, Emp.128.9, A.Ch.650 , Eu.839 , S.OT138, E.HF1155, Hp.Morb.Sacr.1: and in later Prose, as D.S.1.21, SIG985.38 , Porph.Abst.2.11, Dam.Isid.108, Sch.Luc.JTr.8

Μυσός.definition: Mysian, A.Pers.52 , etc.: proverbially feeble and effeminate, whence prov. i. e. a prey to all, of anything that can be plundered with impunity, Stratt.35, D.18.72, Arist.Rh.1372b33; the most worthless of men, Magn.5,…

μύσταξ.definition: Dor. and Lacon. for and always masc., whereas is fem.:—upper lip or moustache, Stratt.65, Eub.113, Theoc.14.4, LXX2 Ki.19.24; the Spartan Ephors on coming into office issued an edict, Arist.Fr.539

μυστηλασία.definition: driving of initiates, Philicus in Stud.Ital.9.45

μύστης.definition: one initiated, Heraclit.14; a name of Dionysus, Paus.8.54.5; of Apollo, Artem.2.70

μύστρον.definition: = Nic.Fr.68.8, cf. Ath.3.126a; spoon, Hippoloch. ap. eund.4.129c, Dsc.3.22, POxy.921.25 , etc.; spoonful, as a dose, Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.28, Herod.Med. ap. eund.8.3.2; alone, as a measure, Gal.13.57, 19.770, Hippiatr…

Μυτιλήνη.definition: Mytilene, the chief city of Lesbos, Hecat.140 J., etc.; Lesb. IG12.1.7:—hence Mytileneans, ib.12.60.1, 17: freq. written corruptly

μύχατος.definition: irreg. Sup. of A.R.1.170, Call.Dian.68, Ps.-Phoc.164, AP9.632; Klio15.48

μυχός.definition: heterocl. pl. Call.Del.142, D.P.117; inmost part of a house, Od.7.96; A.Ch.446 ; . . S.Tr.686; no longer hidden within the house , Id.Ant.1293, cf. E.Tr.299

μώϊον.definition: Egyptian word for a receptacle, box or jar, PHib.1.49.8, PPetr.3p.186 ; PSI4.428.78 ; prob. also a measure of capacity, Ostr.Bodl.i231 : pl. written PCair.Zen.167.7 ; sg. written POxy.146.3 ; cf

μωκός.definition: mocker, Arist.HA491b17, EM593.7: as Adj., LXXSi.36.6

μώλωψ.definition: mark of a stripe, weal, bruise, Hyp.Fr.200, Arist.Pr.889b10, LXXIs.53.5, D.H.16.5, Plu.2.565b, etc.; of an eruption resembling mosquito bites, Herod.Med. ap. Aët.5.129; blood-clot, Paul.Aeg.6.8 ; satirically of kings,…

μῶνυξ.definition: with a single, i.e. uncloven, hoof, epith. of the horse, freq. in Il.,5.236, al.; once in Od.,15.46, cf. Sol.23, E.Ph.793 , Stud.Pont.3.16 ; also Arist.HA499b13; Hp.Art.8; Porph.Abst.4.7; Pl.Plt.265d. and .)

μώριος.definition: = Dsc.4.75.7, Plin.HN21.180; a plant used in philtres, Hsch

μώρωσις.definition: Ion. dullness, sluggishness, Hp.Virg.1; extreme dementia, Id.Prorrh.1.32, Gal.16.696

μαγάδιον.definition: Dim. of BGU1125.21 , Ptol.Harm.1.8,3.1, v.l. in Luc.DDeor.7.4

μάγαδις.definition: gen. Ath.14.634c; nom. pl; a Lydian flute or flageolet, producing a high and a low note together, Ion Trag.23 , Anaxandr. l.c., cf. Did. ap. Ath.14.634e, Hsch. but S.Fr.238 , nisi leg

μαγγανάριος.definition: conjurer, Rhetor.inCat.Cod. Astr.8; mechanical engineer, Papp.1024.14, al

μαγγανεία.definition: trickery, esp. of magical arts, Pl.Lg.908d; ib.933a; Ph.2.267, Gal.11.792; Them.Or.26.330b, cf. Jul.Gal.340a; of meretricious cookery, Ath.1.9c

μαγγάνευμα.definition: trickery, in pl., Pl.Grg.484a, Lg.933c; quack remedies, Max.Tyr.23.3; of women, meretricious arts, Plu.Ant.25

μαγδωλοφυλακία.definition: manning of the watch-tower, dub. in PLond. 3.1235.12 , PRyl.191.5,8

μαγδωλοφύλαξ.definition: guard of the watch-tower, PFay.108.13 , PTeb.353.9 , PLond.3.844.5

μαγειρεῖον.definition: butcher's shop, cook-shop; place where food is cooked, kitchen, IG22.1301 , PCair.Zen.6.55 , PSI6.669.6 , LXXEz.46.23, Explor.Arch. de Délos11.262, Dsc.Eup.1.34, Gal.6.721

μαγείρευμα.definition: that which is cooked, food, Hsch. s.v. , Eust.1402.16

μαγειρίσκιον.definition: Dim. of of a silver cup in the form of a genre figure, Plin.HN33.157

μάγειρος.definition: Dor. IG42.144 , SIG241.16 , IG9.976.7 ; but Att. ib.22.10B2 , and so in Pap. of iii B.C., PCair.Zen.6.48, al., PRev.Laws50.14, both forms freq. in later Inscrr., Pap., and codd.; Aeol. Philox. ap. Et.Gud. in Greg.Cor.…

μαγίς.definition: any kneaded mass, cake; kneading-trough or dresser, Cratin.21, BGU40.8 , cf. Poll.10.81; small table, Epich.118, Cerc.12; also, round pan or plate for placing on the Poll.6.83

μάγμα.definition: thick unguent, Plin.HN13.19, PTeb.273.17 ; esp. an ingredient in the Theriaca Andromachi, Androm. ap. Gal.14.39; also, of a plaster, Id. ap. eund.13.925; cf

μαδαρότης.definition: baldness, Hp.Hum.1, cf. Gal.16.88; falling off of the eyelashes, Id.14.767

μαδάρωσις.definition: falling off of the hair, baldness, Gal.18.55, Vett. Val.109.31 ; esp. from the eyelids, Gal.14.413, Aët.7.80, Paul.Aeg.3.22

μαδάσκομαι.definition: = sq. I, of an ulcer, Steph.in Hp.2.488 D

μαδάω.definition: to be moist or sodden, of a disease in fig-; of hair, fall off, Ael.NA15.18; of persons, to be bald, Ar.Pl.266, Longus3.32, cf. Gal.16.88; Sotionp.186 W.; LXXLe.13.40: abs., if there is baldness, Hp.Mul.2.189

μαζάω.definition: knead a barley-cake, BGU1026 xxii 20; like wax wanton, Suid

μαζίον.definition: Dim. of Phryn.Com.61, Ath.14.646c, Gp.20.33; of the size and shape of a suppository, Hp.Mul.1.78, cf. Dsc.Eup.1.204

μαζονόμον.definition: trencher for serving barley-cakes on, Harmod.1, IG 7.3498.8, 50 , OGI214.50 , prob. in IG22.1478.14:—also POxy.1449.58,60

μάθημα.definition: that which is learnt; learning, knowledge, Ar.Nu.1231, Av.380, Th.2.39, PSI1.94.9 , etc.; educational authorities, SIG578.66 ; the science of tactics, Pl.La.182b: freq. in pl., Isoc.12.27, etc.; Philem.232

μαθηματικεύομαι.definition: employ mathematical reasoning, Dam.Pr.396, cf. Doxop. in Rh.2.132 W

μαθητέος.definition: to be learnt, Pl.Lg.822c; one must learn, Ar.V.1262, Pl.Lg.818d; X.Mem.2.1.28

μαθητεύω.definition: to be pupil, to one, Plu.2.832c; trans., make a disciple of, instruct, Ev.Matt.28.19, cf. Act.Ap.14.21:—Pass., Ev.Matt.13.52

μαθητής.definition: learner, pupil, Hdt.4.77, Mosch.3.95, etc.; of dancing, SIG1094.6 : freq. in Att. of the pupils of philosophers and rhetoricians, Ar.Nu.140; Pl.Prt.315a, al.; Id.Ap.33a: c. gen. rei, a studentofit, Id.R.618c; a studen…

μαθητικεύομαι.definition: make a display of learning, Dam.Pr.192

μαινίδιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Ar.Fr.247, Pherecr.56, Arist.HA569a18

μαινίς.definition: gen. Ar.Ra.985, but Opp.H.1.108:—Dim. of freq. in Com., Ar. l.c., Philyll.27, etc., cf. Arist.HA607b10, Speus. ap. Ath.7.313a, Numen. ap.Ath.7.328d, Dsc.Eup.1.78, Ael.NA12.28, Alciphr.1.6

μαιόομαι.definition: of a midwife, deliver a woman, Call.Jov.35, Luc.DDeor.16.2, cf. Plu.2.999c; AP9.80 ; IG 14.967; of Hephaestus at the birth of Athena, Corn.ND19: abs., practise midwifery, Sor.1.80: in pass. sense, Apollod.1.4.1

μαιριάω.definition: Tarent. for acc. to Hsch. s.v

μακάριος.definition: also Pl.Lg.803c: collat; mostly of men, blessed, happy, Pi.P.5.46, E.Or.86, etc.; Pl.R.335e; ib.354a: distd. from by Arist.EN1101a7, 19: freq. in phrases such as . . Men.114, cf. Mon.357, 614, Phld.Ir.p.3 W.: Sup., Id…

μακαριότης.definition: happiness, bliss, ib.661b, Arist.EN1178b22, Epicur.Ep.1p.28U., etc.; as a title of bishops, Cod.Just.1.3.42 Intr., Just.Nov.3

μακαρισμός.definition: pronouncing happy, blessing, Pl.R.591d, Arist.Rh.1367b33, Andronic.Pass.p.570 M., Plu.2.471c; giving praise or thanks, Epicur.Sent. Vat.52, Phld.D.3 Fr.86a

μακαρίτης.definition: as Adj., with a play on I, Ar.Pl.555

Μακεδονίζω.definition: to be on the Macedonian side, Plb.20.5.5, Plu.Alex.30, etc.: speak Macedonian, Id.Ant.27, Ath.3.122a:—hence Adv. in Macedonian, Plu.Eum.14

μακκοάω.definition: fut. to be stupid, Ar.Eq.396: pf. part. sitting mooning, ib.62, cf. Com.Adesp.1210, Luc.Lex.19.—Derived from a stupid woman, by Suid

μακραυχένοπλος.definition: furnished with long shafts, i. e. oars, Tim.Pers.100

μακραύχην.definition: gen. long-necked, long, E.Ph.1173: neut. pl., Hp.Epid.2.1.8, Arist.HA595a11

μακρηγορέω.definition: speak at great length, be long-winded, A.Th.1057, Hp.Nat.Puer.12, E.Hipp.704, Th.1.68, 2.36, Herod.2.60:—Pass., Porph.Chr.23

μακρήγορος.definition: speaking at great length, Ph.2.268, Tz.H.10.4

μακρημερία.definition: Ion. the season of long days , Hdt.4.86

μακροαπόδοτος.definition: with the apodosis far off, Phlp.in de An.582.32; Eust.1491.49; Sch.D.Tp.114 H

μακροβιότης.definition: longevity, Arist.Rh.1361b32, Gal.14.297, Alex.Aphr.in Top.258.4; of plants, Thphr.HP4.13.2

μακροβολία.definition: a throwing far, a long shot, Str.3.5.1

μακροήμερος.definition: long lived, ib.De.4.40, Anatol.inCat.Cod. Astr.8.188, Eust.129.1: Comp., Philostr.VS2.1.7

μακροθυμέω.definition: to be long-suffering, towards; to be slow to help, Ev.Luc.18.7

μακροθυμία.definition: Ion. long-suffering; forbearance, LXXPr.25.15, Aristeas188. Ep.Eph.4.2

μακρόθυμος.definition: long-suffering, patient, LXXEx.34.6, al.; AP11.317 . Adv. Act.Ap.26.3

μακροκαταληκτέω.definition: end with a long syllable, Choerob.in Theod.2.355 H., Eust.26.36:—Med., Hdn.Gr. in An.Ox.3.229:— hence Did. ap. St.Byz. s.v. A.D.Pron.11.10, al.; Choerob.l.c

μακρόκεντρος.definition: with long sting, Arist.HA532a17; of figs, with long pedicle, Jul.Ep.180

μακροκέφαλος.definition: long-headed, Hp.Epid.2.1.8; of a Scythian tribe, Hes.Fr.62, Hp.Aër.14: Sup., Str.11.11.8

μακρολογέω.definition: speak at length, use many words, Pl.Grg.465b, Tht.163d, Isoc.3.63, Arist.Rh.Al.1440b36, etc.; Hp.Art.43; X.HG4.1.13

μακρολογία.definition: length of speech, opp. Pl.Grg.449c, Prt.335bsq., Arist.Rh.1418b25, Gal.10.425

μακρολόγος.definition: speaking at length, Com.Adesp.14.1 D., cf. Axiop.1.11: Comp., Pl.Sph.268b; Philostr.VS1.10. Adv. Gal.17.744

μακρόμαλλος.definition: with shaggy or long wool, cj. in Str.4.4.3

μακρόπνοια.definition: deep breathing, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.36.4, Gal.7.836

μακροπόνηρος.definition: bearing malice for a long time, Phot

μακροπονία.definition: long labour, v.l. in Aesop.353 Chambry

μακροπρόσωπος.definition: long-faced, PGrenf.2.15 i 12, al. , PLond.3.879 , Peripl.M.Rubr.62, Anatol. in Cat.Cod.Astr.8 .188, etc

μακροπτύστης.definition: spitting far from one, prov. of a 'big bug', Sch.Luc.Nav.15, Apol.7

μακροπώγων.definition: long-bearded, name of a tribe, Str.11.2.1

μακρόσπαρτον.definition: machine drawn by long ropes, cj. for macron sparton , Cael.Aur.TP5.134

μακροσύλλαβος.definition: consisting of long syllables, Phld.Po.Herc.994.31, D.H.Dem.38

μακροτάτω.definition: Adv. Sup. of farthest off, Crates Ep.11, Longus3.17

μακρότης.definition: length, LXXDe.30.20, al.; Phld.Lib.p.28 O.: Gramm. of syllables, A.D.Adv.187.15, Plu.2.947e

μακροτονέω.definition: lengthen the in a torsion-engine; persevere, LXX2 Ma.8.26

μακροφυής.definition: with elongated bodies, Arist.PA696a6 ; of crops, tall, well-grown, PFlor.17.10

μακρόχειρ.definition: long-armed, name of Artaxerxes I, Str.15.3.21, Plu.Art.1; of athletes, Philostr.Gym.31,34

μακρόχηλος.definition: with long hoofs, v.l. in Str.17.3.19

μακροχρόνιος.definition: lasting a long time, lingering; dwelling a long time, LXXEx.20.12, al

μακρύνω.definition: fut. LXXEc.8.13: fut. Pass; lengthen a syllable, Sch.Il.16.390

μαλαβάθρινος.definition: prepared with Crito ap.Gal.12.448, cf. Dsc.1.63; Sor.2.38

μαλάβαθρον.definition: leaf of Cinnamomum Tamala or albiflorum, Peripl.M.Rubr.56, 65, Dsc.1.12, Gal.12.66, Plin.HN12.129. [mālǒbǎthrum Hor.Od.2.7.8.] '.)

μάλαγμα.definition: soft materials, padding, used in sieges to blunt the force of engines and weapons, Ph.Bel.91.7, 95.47; Plu.2.618f, cf. Pl.Ti.70d ap. Longin.32.5; for padding, Ruf. ap. Orib.49.28.10; of a shirt worn under armour, Sch.…

μαλακευνέω.definition: lie on a soft bed, Hp.Insomn.90, prob. in Vict.2.66

μαλακία.definition: weakliness, sickness, LXXGe.42.4, Ev.Matt.4.23, Ps.-Hdt.Vit.Hom.36, POxy.1151.27 ; opp. Phld.Mus.p.30 K

μαλακίζομαι.definition: fut. D.C.38.18: aor; to be softened, appeased, Th.6.29; Id.3.40

μαλακογνώμων.definition: gen. mild of mood, A.Pr.190 ; gloss on Sch.Ar.Ra.82

μαλακοκρανεύς.definition: shrike, Lanius sp., Mod. Gr. Arist.HA617a32

μαλακόχειρ.definition: soft-handed, of a physician's art, Pi.N.3.55

μαλακύνω.definition: soften, v.l. for in Hp.Vict.2.66; Ph.Bel.71.43; LXXJb.23.16; weaken, Muson.Fr.19p.107H.:—Pass., become soft, flag, X.Cyr.3.2.5; D.S.17.10

μαλάσσω.definition: Att. fut. E.Or.1201; of dressing leather, make it supple, Luc.Anach.24; Hp.Aph.5.22, of the human skin:—hence, with reference to Cleon's trade of tanner, give one a hiding, Ar.Eq.388: metaph., worsted in it, Pi.N.3.16…

μαλθακίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be softened, of persons; relax, give in, Pl.R.458b, al.; to be a coward, Id.Smp.179d; to be remiss, Id.Ep.317c

μαλθάσσω.definition: = soften, soothe, A.Pr.381; E.HF298; . . ; why should I soothe thee with fair words ? S.Ant.1194: relax the bowels, Hp.Acut.16, Art.40:—Pass., A.Pr.1008; unnerved by sleep, Id.Eu.134

μαλκίω.definition: become numb with cold, A.Fr.332; D.9.35 ; X.Cyn.5.2 ; Poet. ap. Sch.Nic.Th.382; . . Luc.Lex.2; of a bee in cold weather, Ael.NA5.12, cf. 1.32 ; ib.9.4; ib.16; Them.Or.4.50c; · Phryn.PSp.89 B., cf. Hsch. s. vv. EM*574.…

μάλλωσις.definition: a being clothed with wool, Sch.Pi.P.4.407

μαμμόθρεπτος.definition: brought up by one's grandmother, Sch.Ar.Ra.1021, Aug.in Psalm.30; condemned by Phryn.267, cf. Poll.3.20

μάνδαλος.definition: = II.4, Zeno Med. ap. Erot.s.v. Artem.2.10:—hence Hsch. s.v. with the bolt shot, perh. kiss with the tongue protruded, Phot., cf. Telecl.13: hence, lascivious, . . Ar.Th.132

μανδήλη.definition: = Lat. mantele, towel, Sammelb.7033.42 :— Dim. = Gloss

μανδραγόρας.definition: belladonna, Atropa Belladonna, Thphr.HP6.2.9; epith. of Zeus, Hsch

μανδραγοριζομένη.definition: the mandrake-drugged, title of play by Alexis:—Act. in Suid

μανδραγορίτης.definition: flavoured with mandrake, Dsc.5.71:—fem. epith. of Aphrodite. Hsch

μανιάκης.definition: necklace, torc, worn of gold by Persians and Gauls, Plb.2.29.8, 2.31.5, LXX1 Es.3.6, Plu.Cim.9, Jul.ad Ath.284d, Lyd.Mag.1.46 :—also PMon.7.74 :—Dim. Sch.Theoc.11.41

μαντεῖος.definition: also E.Ion130 ; Ion. for oracular, prophetic, Pi.O.6.5, P.5.69, etc.; A.Ag.1265; E.l.c.; Pae.Delph.18; of the altar's embers, S.OT21; i.e.Apollo, E.Tr.454, cf. Or.1666, Ar.Av.722

μάντευμα.definition: oracle, Pi.P.4.73, S.OT992, E.Med.685, etc.: pl., Pi.P.8.60, Pae.7.1, Pl.Ep.311d, Supp.Epigr.3.400 , etc

μαντιπόλος.definition: frenzied, inspired, E.Hec.121 ; Orac. ap. Luc.JTr.31: pl., as Subst., diviners, Man.6.306

μαντοσύνη.definition: the art of divination, Il.1.72, Pi.O.6.66, Luc.Astr.1: pl., Il.2.832, 11.330, Emp.112.10, Man.6.317

μαππίον.definition: Dim. of Lat. mappa, napkin, POxy.1051.17 , Gloss

μαραθοειδής.definition: like fennel, v.l. for in Dsc.3.139. Adv. v.l. for in Id.2.139

μάραθον.definition: fennel, Foeniculum vulgare, D.18.260, Anaxandr.41.58, Thphr.HP1.12.2, al.: pl., Epich.156, 159:—also Python1.13, but Lyd.Mag.1.42; of doubtful gender, Hermipp.81, Lycus ap.Orib.8.32.4

Μαραθωνομάχης.definition: one who fought at Marathon: prov. of a veteran, Ar.Ach.181, Nu.986:—also APl.4.233.8 , D.L.1.56, and v.l. Ar.Nu.l.c

μαργαρίδης.definition: Ion. for Praxag. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.22 B

μαργάω.definition: only in part. raging, esp. in battle, A.Th.380; S.Fr.842; E.HF1005; Id.Hec.1128; Id.Hipp.1230, cf. Call.Fr.98a; ravenous jaw, A.Fr.258: c. inf., madly eager to . . , E.Ph.1247

Μαργίτης.definition: Margites, i. e. madman, hero of a mock-heroic poem of the same name, ascribed to Homer, Arist.Po.1448b30, etc

μάργος.definition: of appetite, greedy, gluttonous, Od.18.2; E.Cyc.310: metaph., Emp.100.7; Phryn.Trag.5.4

μαργοσύνη.definition: gluttony, Anacr.87, Luc.Epigr.2.10; lust, wantonness, Thgn.1271 , A.R.3.797, al

μεσσόθεν.definition: poet. for Adv. from the middle, Parm.8.44, cf. A.R.1.1168: c. gen., AP9.661 ; Ti.Locr.95e

μέσφα.definition: Adv., poet. for until, c. gen; before even till . . , c. aor. ind., Call.Dian.195, Hec.1.1.4: without as a Conj., until, c. ind., Id.Cer.93, A.R.2.1227, AP7.614.10 : c. subj., D.P.586; Opp.H.1.754; while, Cerc.4.49

μεταδρομάδην.definition: Adv. running after, following close upon, Il.5.80, A.R.1.755, Opp.H.4.509

μέταζε.definition: Adv., = to be read in Hes.Op.394, cf. Hdn. Gr.2.951, Sch.Il.3.29, Sch.D.T.p.278 H.; but Hsch

μεταῦθις.definition: Ion. Adv. afterwards, thereupon, A.Eu.478, 498 , Hdt.1.62

μετέπειτα.definition: Adv. afterwards, thereafter, Il.14.310, Od.10.519, al., Hdt.1.25, 3.36, 7.7, 197: rare in early Prose, Pl.Ep.353c, cf. Arist.EN1175a9; later, OGI177.14 , LXXJu.9.5, 3 Ma.3.24, Ep.Hebr.12.17

μετωπηδόν.definition: Adv. with front foremost; of ships, forming a close front, in line, Hdt.7.100; opp. , Th.2.90; Plb.11.22.10, cf.Ph.2.354, Plu.Lys.10

μηδαμά.definition: Adv. of of Time, = and of Manner, not at all, freq. in Hdt. with another or compd. of 1.68; never anything, 7.50; 3.65; . . A.Pers.431, cf. Pr.526 , S.OC517 , 1104, 1698 ; Ar.Th.1162; SIG45.39 : with tmesis, prob. in …

μηδαμόθεν.definition: Adv. of from no place, X.Cyr.8.7.14; from no other place, Pl.Phd.70e, GDIiv p.876 , etc.; Lat. nullius filius, D.21.148

μηδαμοῦ.definition: Adv. nowhere, Th.1.35, Pl.Lg.958d; Id.Phd.68a: c. gen., Lat. nusquam gentium, Id.Prm.162c: metaph., is of no account, A.Eu.423, cf. 624, S.Aj.1007; X.Mem.1.2.52: as two words, IG12.16.11

μηδαμῶς.definition: Adv. of = Hdt.4.83, A.Pr.339, S.OC278; Pl.Lg.838d: in replies, as a strong neg., Id.Prt.334d, Men.Sam.217

μηδετέρωθεν.definition: Adv. from neither side, Corn.ND17, Lib.Decl.1.9

μηδετέρωσε.definition: Adv. to neither side, Hp.Superf.4, Th.4.118, Paus.2.1.4

μηκέτι.definition: Adv., no more, no longer, no further, Il.13.292, Hes.Op.174, Pi.O.1.5, A.Ch.805 , IG12.75.29, etc

μητρόθεν.definition: from one's mother, A.Ch.750, cf. Ar.Ach.478; from one's mother's womb, A.Th.664, cf. Ch.607 : with the force of a gen., . . S.OC527 .— Poet. word, used by Hdt., and in later Prose, Luc.Tox.51, Alex.11, Arch.Pap.2.444 …

μίνυνθα.definition: Adv. a short time, in Hom. mostly in phrase, Il.1.416, Od.22.473; but short-lived was his effort, Il.4.466; Od.15.494; Mimn.2.7; B.5.151; A.R.4.1060

μιξολυδιστί.definition: Adv. in the mixolydian mode, Pl.R.398e, Arist.Pol.1340b1

μόγις.definition: Aeol. Jo.Gramm.Comp.3.10: Adv., with toil and pain, i. e. hardly, scarcely, Il.9.355, Od.3.119, Hdt.1.116, Ev.Luc.9.39, etc.; Lys.22.10; A.Pr.131 ; Id.Pers.509; Pl.Com.31; Pl.Prt.360d; Id.Chrm.155e; Charito1.8; Pl.Phd…

μοναχόθεν.definition: Adv. from one side only, Suid. s.v

μονόθεν.definition: Adv. alone, singly, Hdt.1.116; on one side only, Sch.Arat.8

μυκηδόν.definition: Adv. with bellowings, Poet. in POxy.864.22

μυκτηρόθεν.definition: Adv. out of the nose, AP10.75

μυριάκις.definition: Adv., ten thousand times, numberless times, Ar.Nu.738, Ra.63, Pl.Lg.677d, Arist.Metaph.1007a16

μυριαχοῦ.definition: Adv. in ten thousand places or passages, Phld.D.3 Fr.2, Zonae.Fig.10, Eust.47.29, 76.19

μυριοπάλαι.definition: Adv. time out of mind, Eust.725.40; cf
